title: The Counsel Etched in Wisdom
intro: Imagine standing beside a figure known not for miracles or kingdoms, but for words that still guide hearts today. This servant of Allah received a precious gift and poured gratitude into every counsel given to a beloved young learner.
clues: I was blessed by Allah with wisdom, and I was commanded to be grateful for it.
I spoke to my son with tender admonition, warning with love and concern.
I told my son that associating partners with Allah is a tremendous wrong.
I advised my son to establish prayer, enjoin right, forbid wrong, and bear with patience.
I warned my son not to turn the cheek in pride nor to walk upon the earth in arrogance.
I taught my son to be moderate in pace and to lower the voice, for the harshest of sounds is the braying of donkeys.

identity.label: Who Am I?
options: Dhul-Kifl the Patient
Luqman the Wise
The Man of the Two Gardens
Tubba the Ruler
Khidr the Guide

trial.label: My Greatest Counsel
options: Advising my child against associating partners with Allah
Building an ark to survive the great flood
Interpreting the ruler's dream while in prison
Confronting Pharaoh with miraculous signs
Being swallowed by a great fish in the sea
trial.answer: Advising my child against associating partners with Allah

location.label: Gift Granted to Me
options: A staff that became a serpent
Wisdom and gratitude to Allah
A throne carried in the blink of an eye
An ark of gopher wood
A garden of date-palms and vines

outcome.label: How I Am Remembered
options: As one drowned in the flood for disbelief
As one swallowed by the earth for pride
As a model of gratitude and wise parental counsel
As one destroyed by a mighty blast from the sky
As one transformed for breaking the Sabbath
outcome.answer: As a model of gratitude and wise parental counsel

arabic: وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا لُقْمَـٰنَ ٱلْحِكْمَةَ أَنِ ٱشْكُرْ لِلَّهِ ۚ وَمَن يَشْكُرْ فَإِنَّمَا يَشْكُرُ لِنَفْسِهِۦ ۖ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِىٌّ حَمِيدٌۭ
verse: And We had certainly given Luqmān wisdom [and said], "Be grateful to Allāh." And whoever is grateful is grateful for [the benefit of] himself. And whoever denies [His favor] - then indeed, Allāh is Free of need and Praiseworthy. (31:12)
